title: Equivalent notions of satisfiability
statement: Let $q$ be a positive integer and let $G$ be a finite unique game with a nonempty set of variables and a nonempty set of constraints. Each constraint joins two distinct variables, carries a permutation of the $q$ labels, and every variable occurs in some constraint. Then $G$ has a labeling satisfying every constraint if and only if the associated constraint satisfaction instance has optimum value $1$.
hypotheses_covered: The variable set is finite and nonempty
The constraint set is finite and nonempty
Each constraint carries a permutation of the labels
Every variable participates in a constraint
